xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4507: Issue poller: back off when nothing changes instead of polling every repo every 30 s

plan.title: Issue poller: back off when nothing changes instead of polling every repo every 30 s
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: IssueDataService polls GitHub every 30 s with two listForRepo calls per configured repo (about 960 requests an hour for four repos). ETag 304s are free against quota, but the interval only grows under rate-limit pressure, never when nothing changed.
narratives.Proposal: Track a per-tracker unchanged streak for GitHub. Each scheduled poll that returns unchanged data doubles the interval from 30 s up to the existing 300 s max; a changed poll, an operator refresh (invalidateTracker, cache clear), a GET /api/issues read, or a verified GitHub issues webhook resets it to 30 s without deleting ETags. The delay math lives in a new pure module (poll-cadence.ts) combined with the existing rate-limit backoff, suspension and PAT quota pause; /api/cache-status reports the interval, the reason, the streak and the next poll time. A preparatory extraction keeps issue-data-service.ts under its file-size cap.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Backing off Linear or Rally polling
- Hooking the WS getSnapshot bootstrap in ws-rpc.ts
- Configuring GitHub App event subscriptions from code
- Resetting cadence on check_run, status, pull_request*, or issue_comment webhooks
- Changing getBackoffMs multipliers, the 300 s max, ETag handling, or the per-poll request count
- Raising any file-size allowlist row
- Any frontend change

autoDecisions.summary: Back off GitHub only; Linear and Rally keep today's cadence.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue scopes the GitHub poller and its reset triggers are GitHub webhooks; Linear has no webhook reset and its own 5-minute full-refresh safety net.

autoDecisions.summary: Interval = min(30 s x 2^streak, 300 s), combined as max(unchanged, rate-limit), then suspension, then quota pause; the startup poll never advances the streak.
autoDecisions.rationale: Produces exactly the issue's 30-60-120-240-300 sequence and preserves every existing rate-limit and PAN-4264 behavior.

autoDecisions.summary: Report five interval reasons (default, unchanged-backoff, rate-limit-backoff, rate-limit-suspended, quota-pause) instead of three.
autoDecisions.rationale: Suspension and the PAT quota pause already set the delay; folding them into another label would make /api/cache-status misreport why the poller waits.

autoDecisions.summary: 'Opening the issue list' maps to GET /api/issues; the WS getSnapshot bootstrap is not hooked.
autoDecisions.rationale: The Kanban list arrives over the WS snapshot, but ws-rpc.ts sits one line under its file-size cap; the Refresh button already resets and worst-case staleness equals the existing 300 s max.

autoDecisions.summary: Webhook reset uses a new resetPollCadence (re-arm at <=30 s) on 'issues' events only, never invalidateTracker.
autoDecisions.rationale: invalidateTracker deletes ETags so every poll would become a paid 200; check_run/status/pull_request events fire constantly and would pin the cadence at 30 s.

autoDecisions.summary: Extract the pure status-mapping helpers to a new module before wiring the feature.
autoDecisions.rationale: issue-data-service.ts is exactly at its 1754-line allowlist cap and agents may not raise it.

Add pure poll-cadence module with POLL_INTERVALS and computePollDelay

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2. Create src/dashboard/server/services/poll-cadence.ts exporting POLL_INTERVALS (same values as today's const in issue-data-service.ts), PollIntervals, PollIntervalReason ('default'|'unchanged-backoff'|'rate-limit-backoff'|'rate-limit-suspended'|'quota-pause'), MAX_SUSPENSION_MS = 3_600_000, unchangedBackoffMs(intervals, streak) = min(default * 2^max(0,streak), max), and computePollDelay({intervals, unchangedStreak, rateBackoffMs, suspendMs, quotaPauseMs}) -> {delayMs, reason}. Formula (PRD Decision 2): unchangedMs as above; rateMs = min(max(default+rateBackoffMs, min), max); delay = max(unchangedMs, rateMs); if suspendMs>0 delay = min(suspendMs, MAX_SUSPENSION_MS); then delay = max(delay, quotaPauseMs). Reason precedence (Decision 3): quota-pause if quotaPauseMs set the final delay (quotaPauseMs > pre-pause delay); else rate-limit-suspended if suspendMs>0; else rate-limit-backoff if rateMs>default and rateMs>=unchangedMs; else unchanged-backoff if unchangedMs>default; else default. No I/O, no timers. Write the pure unit tests listed in PRD WI-2.

Given quotaPauseMs 500000 and streak 4, when computePollDelay runs, then it returns delayMs 500000 with reason quota-pause; with quotaPauseMs 1000 it returns 300000 with reason unchanged-backoff

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3, steps 1-6 exactly. Delete the local POLL_INTERVALS const and import POLL_INTERVALS/computePollDelay/PollIntervalReason from ./poll-cadence.js. Add TrackerState fields unchangedStreak (0), intervalReason ('default'), nextPollAt (null), cadenceGeneration (0). pollGitHub/pollGitHubRepos return Promise<boolean|null>: null on PAT-pause or no-config early return, else the computed `changed`. scheduleNext: clear any armed timer first, compute the delay via computePollDelay (quotaPauseMs = patRestPauseDelayMs() for github, 0 otherwise), store intervalReason, currentInterval and nextPollAt = Date.now()+delay; keep the suspension console.warn; in the cache-read catch path fall back to default and still apply the github PAT pause. Timer callback: first set state.timer=null and nextPollAt=null, capture cadenceGeneration, then for github: changed===true -> streak 0; changed===false and generation unchanged -> streak+1; null/throw -> leave streak. invalidateTracker sets unchangedStreak=0 right before its scheduleNext. Startup poll in start() never advances the streak. Create the test file modeled on issue-data-service-quota.test.ts (hoisted Octokit mock whose paginate returns [] = unchanged, fake timers, temp OVERDECK_HOME) with the cases in PRD WI-3. Use vi.useFakeTimers + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync only; no real waits; no source-reading assertions. In the tracker-config.js mock override getGitHubConfig AND getLinearApiKey: () => null AND getRallyConfig: () => null so no test touches a real Linear or Rally API.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5 and Decision 6. Add public resetPollCadence(tracker): unchangedStreak=0; cadenceGeneration++; if this.started and state.timer and state.nextPollAt !== null and state.nextPollAt - Date.now() > POLL_INTERVALS[tracker].default, then clearTimeout, state.timer=null, scheduleNext(tracker); otherwise leave the timer. It must never poll and never call cache.invalidate. clearCacheAndRefresh(): after pushSnapshot(), call resetPollCadence for github, linear and rally. routes/issues.ts GET /api/issues: call issueDataService.resetPollCadence('github') right after `const issueDataService = getIssueDataService();`. Add the WI-5 service tests (do not add source-grep tests). No GET /api/issues route-test harness exists (checked tests/unit/dashboard/routes and src/dashboard/server/routes/__tests__), so FR-4 is covered by the service-level resetPollCadence tests plus typecheck; do not build a new route harness for one line. The tracker-config.js mock must return null for getLinearApiKey and getRallyConfig because clearCacheAndRefresh polls all three trackers. The re-armed delay is the current rate-limit-adjusted interval at streak 0 (30 s when there is no rate-limit pressure).
